issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must have domestic relations jurisdiction over divorce, custody, support, and property division.

issues.label: Personal jurisdiction/service
issues.why: The court must ensure proper service and personal jurisdiction over both parties and any joined third parties.

issues.label: Venue propriety
issues.why: The divorce and related claims must be filed in the proper county/venue under applicable rules.

issues.label: Final appealable order compliance
issues.why: The court must enter a single final judgment resolving all required Civ.R. 75(F) matters to be appealable under R.C. 2505.02.

issues.label: Civ.R. 75(F) single judgment
issues.why: All property division orders and related monetary judgments must be incorporated into one decree/judgment as required.

issues.label: Scope of remand mandate
issues.why: On remand, the court must follow Moore II instructions and may not revisit issues outside the mandate.

issues.label: Law-of-the-case doctrine
issues.why: Prior appellate determinations (what was affirmed, reversed, or mooted) bind the trial court on remand.

issues.label: Jurisdiction to modify property
issues.why: The court must determine whether it has authority to alter the property division beyond the remanded corrections.

issues.label: Jurisdiction to modify support
issues.why: The court must distinguish remand recalculation of support from post-decree modification requiring change of circumstances.

issues.label: Magistrate authority/procedure
issues.why: If magistrate decisions are used, the court must follow Civ.R. 53 procedures, review, and objections standards.

issues.label: Due process on remand
issues.why: The court must ensure each party had a meaningful opportunity to present evidence/argument on remanded issues.

issues.label: Evidentiary hearing necessity
issues.why: The court must decide whether statutes or due process require an evidentiary hearing versus record-only determination.

issues.label: Discovery entitlement on remand
issues.why: The court must decide whether updated financial discovery is permissible/required given remand scope and statutory needs inquiry.

issues.label: Admissibility of new evidence
issues.why: The court must decide whether to accept post-trial evidence (income/lifestyle/needs) or confine itself to the trial record.

issues.label: Correct statutory version
issues.why: The court must apply the correct version of R.C. 3119.04 and related provisions in effect for the relevant period.

issues.label: Child support statutory framework
issues.why: The court must use R.C. 3119.04 (not the basic schedule worksheet) for combined incomes exceeding the statutory maximum.

issues.label: Determine combined income
issues.why: Even under R.C. 3119.04, the court must identify and support findings on both parents’ incomes or earning abilities.

issues.label: Income definition accuracy
issues.why: The court must correctly classify wages, bonuses, dividends, stock, and other compensation as “income” under child support law.

issues.label: Treatment of variable compensation
issues.why: The court must decide how to average or annualize Robert’s large bonuses/stock/dividend income and explain methodology.

issues.label: Self-employment income proof
issues.why: The court must determine April’s income from her law practice and whether claimed business expenses are legitimate.

issues.label: Imputation vs estimation
issues.why: The court must clarify whether it is imputing income (and satisfy statutory prerequisites) or estimating income from evidence.

issues.label: Credibility and findings
issues.why: If rejecting a party’s financial evidence, the court must make supportable credibility determinations and findings.

issues.label: R.C. 3119.04 needs analysis
issues.why: The court must base support on the child’s needs and the parents’ standard of living for high-income cases.

issues.label: Standard-of-living determination
issues.why: The court must determine the lifestyle the child would have enjoyed and the parents’ living standards absent divorce.

issues.label: Allocate shared-parenting costs
issues.why: The court must account for the shared parenting plan and each household’s expenditures and time allocation.

issues.label: Consider child-specific expenses
issues.why: The court must identify which expenses are for the child (e.g., nanny, school, travel) versus the parent’s personal lifestyle.

issues.label: Nanny expense treatment
issues.why: The court must decide whether and how nanny/childcare costs factor into the support amount and/or separate allocations.

issues.label: School tuition allocation
issues.why: The court must decide responsibility for private school tuition consistent with R.C. 3119 factors and best interests.

issues.label: Health insurance allocation
issues.why: The court must allocate health insurance and cash medical support consistent with statutory requirements and worksheet conventions.

issues.label: Extraordinary medical allocation
issues.why: The court must allocate extraordinary/uninsured medical expenses and specify percentages and definitions.

issues.label: Extracurricular expense allocation
issues.why: The court must define and allocate extracurricular and other add-on expenses and avoid ambiguity.

issues.label: Deviation findings sufficiency
issues.why: Any deviation upward or downward must be justified with findings tied to statutory factors and the evidence.

issues.label: Less-than-maximum findings
issues.why: If awarding less than the schedule maximum, R.C. 3119.04(B) requires specific findings that the amount is unjust/inappropriate.

issues.label: Worksheet use limits
issues.why: The court must avoid using the R.C. 3119.021 worksheet as determinative for high-income support, using it only as reference if appropriate.

issues.label: Support amount rationality
issues.why: The court must ensure the $8,500 figure is supported by evidence and reasoning rather than arbitrary selection.

issues.label: Effective date consistency
issues.why: The court must resolve conflicting statements about retroactivity and clearly set a lawful effective date.

issues.label: Retroactive support authority
issues.why: The court must determine the extent to which it may make the new support order retroactive and under what legal basis.

issues.label: Temporary vs final support interplay
issues.why: The court must reconcile temporary orders and the final order to compute arrears or overpayments correctly.

issues.label: CSEA role and delegation
issues.why: The court must avoid improper delegation to CSEA while permitting administrative recalculations consistent with the decree.

issues.label: Overpayment determination method
issues.why: Any finding of overpayment must be computed accurately from payment records and valid orders.

issues.label: Recoupment mechanism legality
issues.why: The court must decide whether reducing future support to recoup overpayment is permissible and in the child’s best interest.

issues.label: Gift vs support characterization
issues.why: The court must classify payments as child support versus gifts for enforceability, tax, and recoupment consequences.

issues.label: Non-child-support reimbursements
issues.why: The court must distinguish child support from reimbursements for bills or other obligations under temporary orders.

issues.label: Child’s best interest in recoupment
issues.why: Repayment or offset orders must not undermine the child’s current needs and welfare.

issues.label: Arrearage interest issues
issues.why: The court must consider whether statutory interest applies to arrears/overpayments and how it is calculated.

issues.label: Contempt/enforcement implications
issues.why: Support changes and offsets affect any enforcement or contempt matters and must be consistent with enforceable orders.

issues.label: Tax consequences of support
issues.why: The court must consider how allocations (tuition, insurance, reimbursements) interact with tax treatment and exemptions if relevant.

issues.label: Property classification standards
issues.why: The court must classify each asset/debt as marital or separate under R.C. 3105.171 with supporting findings.

issues.label: De facto termination date use
issues.why: The court must correctly apply the January 30, 2016 (or specified) de facto date for valuation/classification where appropriate.

issues.label: Valuation date for New Albany
issues.why: Per Moore II, the court must establish New Albany’s value as of the de facto termination date and adjust allocations.

issues.label: New Albany market-loss allocation
issues.why: The court must decide equitably how any post-termination market change and sale delay affects each party.

issues.label: New Albany sale-delay responsibility
issues.why: The court must consider whether either party’s conduct (e.g., pricing refusal) warrants equitable adjustment or credits.

issues.label: New Albany separate-property percentage
issues.why: The court must correctly compute Robert’s separate interest arising from the purchase funds’ separate component.

issues.label: New Albany sale expense credits
issues.why: The court must decide credits for repairs, carrying costs, and sale-related expenses supported by evidence/stipulations.

issues.label: Enforce stipulations
issues.why: The court must honor and properly implement party stipulations (e.g., $35,000 repairs; $30,000 fee offset) unless invalid.

issues.label: Setoff accounting accuracy
issues.why: The court must accurately apply offsets (fees, reimbursements) to each party’s share without double counting.

issues.label: Correct Vero Beach correction
issues.why: The court must correct the Robert’s Vero Beach award using the stipulated marital interest and avoid reopening affirmed parts.

issues.label: Debt allocation corrections
issues.why: The court must split the jet debt, tax payment, and account withdrawal 50/50 as mandated and reflect it in totals.

issues.label: Debt characterization as marital
issues.why: The court must confirm the jet services debt and other obligations are marital and properly allocated.

issues.label: Tracing separate property
issues.why: Where separate property is claimed, the court must apply tracing rules and burdens of proof.

issues.label: Commingling/transmutation issues
issues.why: The court must decide whether commingled funds lost separate character or remain traceable.

issues.label: Equitable distribution factors
issues.why: The overall division must be equitable under R.C. 3105.171(C) considering statutory factors and circumstances.

issues.label: Distributive awards justification
issues.why: Any distributive award or unequal division must be explained with findings supporting equity.

issues.label: Valuation of other assets
issues.why: Even if not reopened, the court must ensure corrected components integrate consistently with previously valued assets.

issues.label: Treatment of bonuses/stock in property
issues.why: The court must distinguish compensation as income for support versus marital property for division, avoiding double counting.

issues.label: Double-dipping avoidance
issues.why: The court must avoid counting the same stream of funds both as marital property and as income for support without analysis.

issues.label: Post-decree lump-sum judgments
issues.why: Reducing obligations to judgment requires authority, correct amounts, and clarity about enforceability and execution.

issues.label: Interest on property judgments
issues.why: The court must decide statutory interest on monetary property awards and the start date for interest.

issues.label: Attorney fee orders finality
issues.why: Although affirmed, the court must ensure attorney-fee awards are properly incorporated and not altered beyond jurisdiction.

issues.label: Spousal support waiver effect
issues.why: The court must enforce April’s 2016 waiver and address whether later motions can revive spousal support claims.

issues.label: Restraint order modification authority
issues.why: The court must decide whether modifying restraining orders and permitting custodial withdrawals is within its authority.

issues.label: Custodial accounts governance
issues.why: The court must identify the legal nature of the custodial accounts (e.g., UTMA) and permissible withdrawals for the child.

issues.label: Necessary parties dismissal
issues.why: Dismissing the custodian must not impair adjudication of account rights or violate due process.

issues.label: Accounting for custodial withdrawals
issues.why: The court must consider whether withdrawals affect support/expense allocations or require safeguards/accounting.

issues.label: Shared parenting decree integration
issues.why: The final order must integrate financial terms with the shared parenting plan without conflict or ambiguity.

issues.label: Clarity and enforceability
issues.why: Support, offsets, percentages, and responsibilities must be stated clearly enough to be enforceable and administrable.

issues.label: Findings of fact adequacy
issues.why: The court must make sufficient findings to permit appellate review on remand issues (support, valuation, allocations).

issues.label: Abuse of discretion standards
issues.why: The court must apply the correct discretionary standards for support and property so the order survives appellate review.

issues.label: Equal protection/consistency concerns
issues.why: The court must apply statutes consistently and avoid arbitrary disparate treatment between similarly situated parties.

issues.label: Sanctions/frivolous conduct impact
issues.why: If prior findings of frivolous reimbursement claims affect fees or credibility, the court must apply proper legal standards.

issues.label: Contempt and sanctions jurisdiction
issues.why: Any ongoing contempt/sanctions issues must be resolved or clearly severed so as not to defeat finality.

issues.label: Parentage collateral issues
issues.why: Any parentage determinations must be resolved or confirmed as not impacting support for the 2014 child.

issues.label: Effective incorporation by reference
issues.why: If the court incorporates multiple entries by reference, it must do so in a way that forms one coherent final judgment.

issues.label: Mathematical reconciliation
issues.why: All corrected property and debt allocations must be arithmetically reconciled to avoid inconsistent totals.
